unit: connectors joining each zone to the network
why: one connector makes a zone's whole demand enter the network at a single node, which turns the access point into a bottleneck that is not real - the largest office zone in Inaquito was loading a one-way street at four times capacity. connect_mode picks the N nodes nearest the centroid, so this spreads the demand but does not choose where it spreads to

unit: road classes a stranded zone may be joined to
why: connect_mode only joins a centroid to a node inside its own zone, which leaves a few stranded on islands or in one-way traps; they are joined to the nearest node on a road of these classes instead, since a slightly longer connector is closer to the truth than none

unit: free-flow km/h by OSM road class
why: no speed survey; typical urban values, used only where OSM has no maxspeed tag

unit: (free-flow km/h at least, vehicles per hour per lane per direction)
why: what limits a road is whether traffic has to stop. Nothing interrupts a grade-separated road, so a lane carries what car-following allows, about 2,000/h. A signalised street discharges at a similar rate but only while the light is green, so it carries about half that. OSM does not say which a road is, and its class tag is not reliable - `trunk` covers both Simon Bolivar at 90 km/h and 575 links at 60 or below. Speed is the usable proxy: you cannot post 90 km/h on a road with traffic lights. Rates are textbook, the speed that selects them is data. The lower bands matter as much as the upper: they cover 103,184 of the 116,697 links, and lumping them together washes out the difference between a service road and a through street

unit: lanes per direction where OSM does not say
why: used only where the lanes tag is missing; how often that happens is printed below

unit: km/h and veh/h on centroid connectors
why: a connector is not a road; an unlimited one keeps zone-system artefacts out of the queues

unit: km/h and veh/h per lane for an unlisted class
why: the speed stands in for a class the table below does not list, and the check after it fails loudly if that happens. The capacity is unreachable in practice - the speed bands start at zero, so every link finds one

unit: how lopsided a zone must be to get another connector
why: the ratio of a zone's share of the city's travel to the share of road capacity where it joins the network. At 4 a zone is carrying four times the traffic its access points are built for

unit: how far an extra connector may reach
why: far enough to find the arterial on a zone's edge, short enough that a zone still joins the network near its own people

unit: intrazonal cost as a share of the trip to the nearest other zone
why: a skim has no diagonal; without one every zone is its own best destination and the trip matrix collapses onto itself

unit: person trips per resident per peak hour
why: no household travel survey; a typical peak share of a 2.5-3.5 trip day

unit: relative pull per m2 of floor area
why: no establishment register and no employment data; shops pull hardest, industry least. Only the ratios matter - the totals are rescaled to match productions

unit: share of person trips made by car
why: MEASURED, not assumed: the Municipio puts private vehicles at 19% of trips today, and aims for 3% by 2042 (Secretaria de Movilidad, reported in Primicias, 8 Jan 2024). This replaces a guess of 0.35, which gave 208% more travel time than free flow and was already cut to 0.20 on the grounds that no working city shows that - a correction the official figure then confirmed to within a point
MEASURED, not assumed: the Municipio de Quito puts the average at 1.3 people per car (Alcalde Pabel Munoz, reported in Primicias, 8 Jan 2024). Was 1.5 by guesswork
no observed trip length distribution; this sets the deterrence parameter, which is solved for rather than guessed
EXPO needs one parameter where GAMMA needs two, and nothing here would justify the second

unit: alpha and beta in the BPR volume-delay function
why: no observed speed-flow data for Quito's streets; these are the values BPR is almost always published with, and the ones the scenarios notebook uses

unit: peak-hour trips a person makes on a working day
why: one out and one back; nothing in the data says so
a common figure for a five-day year less holidays; not specific to Quito
